slides.title: Unfolding makes parameter sharing visible
points: h(t) = φ( Wxh x(t) + Whh h(t-1) + b )
Wxh maps the current input into hidden state.
Whh carries information from the previous hidden state.
The same weights are reused across sequence positions.
slides.takeaway: Wxh maps the current input into hidden state.
slides.formula: h(t) = φ( Wxh x(t) + Whh h(t-1) + b )

slides.title: Backpropagation through time trains unfolded recurrent graphs
points: Forward through time
The RNN reads sequence elements one by one, updating hidden state and producing outputs.
Backward through time
Errors are propagated backward across the unfolded graph so shared recurrent weights receive accumulated gradients.
slides.takeaway: The RNN reads sequence elements one by one, updating hidden state and producing outputs.

slides.title: Recurrent neural networks keep a hidden state
points: Memory mechanism
The hidden state acts as a summary of previous inputs, allowing the model to condition current predictions on earlier context.
Use cases
RNNs are used for language modeling, tagging, sentiment analysis, speech, forecasting, and other sequence tasks.
slides.takeaway: The hidden state acts as a summary of previous inputs, allowing the model to condition current predictions on earlier context.

slides.title: Standard RNNs struggle with long-range dependencies
points: Gradients repeatedly pass through recurrent connections across many time steps.
They can shrink, making early information hard to learn from.
They can also grow, causing unstable updates.
Gated RNNs such as LSTMs were designed to manage these problems better.
slides.takeaway: Gradients repeatedly pass through recurrent connections across many time steps.
slides.formula: Gradients repeatedly pass through recurrent connections across many time steps.

slides.title: Bidirectional context helps when the full sequence is available
points: Why it helps
A prediction at position t can use information from earlier and later positions, not only the past.
Where it fits
Bidirectional RNNs are useful for tagging, sequence labeling, and text understanding tasks where the whole input sequence is known.
slides.takeaway: A prediction at position t can use information from earlier and later positions, not only the past.

slides.title: Recursive neural networks process tree structures
points: root
Unlike an RNN over a line of time steps, a recursive net composes representations according to a tree.
slides.takeaway: Unlike an RNN over a line of time steps, a recursive net composes representations according to a tree.

slides.title: Recursive nets fit compositional structure
points: Where they help
They can model parse trees, expression trees, hierarchical documents, and nested structures.
Core operation
Child representations are combined to form a parent representation, and this repeats upward through the tree.
slides.takeaway: They can model parse trees, expression trees, hierarchical documents, and nested structures.

slides.title: Gated RNNs reduce the long-dependency problem
points: Plain RNN
Repeated multiplication through many time steps can weaken or destabilize gradient signals.
Gated RNN
Gates create controlled paths for remembering, forgetting, and exposing information, making long-range dependency learning easier.
slides.takeaway: Repeated multiplication through many time steps can weaken or destabilize gradient signals.

slides.title: Training sequence models requires care over time
points: Backpropagation through time can be computationally expensive for long sequences.
Gradients may vanish or explode across many recurrent steps.
Truncating the time horizon trades efficiency for limited long-range credit assignment.
Gating, careful initialization, clipping, and batching are common practical aids.
slides.takeaway: Backpropagation through time can be computationally expensive for long sequences.
slides.formula: Gradients may vanish or explode across many recurrent steps.
